implementation_notes: Kotlin absorbs the holder into property delegation: 'val author: Author by lazy { gateway.find(authorId) }' runs the lambda on the first get() and remembers the result, with SYNCHRONIZED (the default) computing the value in one thread while every reader sees it, PUBLICATION letting threads execute the initializer simultaneously, and NONE dropping synchronization. The stdlib documents that an exception from the initializer is not cached - the next access attempts to re-initialize - and that a lazy delegate in a companion object is initialized once per class, not once per instance. The classic proxy/holder class is unnecessary in Kotlin; JPA associations on the JVM side remain the framework alternative for mapped entities.
pitfalls: SYNCHRONIZED (the default) blocks every reader while the initializer runs, and the stdlib warns against locking the Lazy instance from outside - a slow database read in the initializer stalls all threads that touch the property.

A throwing initializer is not cached: the next access re-runs the load, so failure semantics differ from .NET's Lazy<T> and must be chosen deliberately (never let the initializer recurse into the same property).
Delegated properties have no backing field until loaded, so JPA/Java serialization and reflection-based mapping may not see them; and a lazy delegate in a companion object is once per class.
